sections.title: Fine-tuned models or LLMs — chosen on accuracy and cost

blocks.heading: When fine-tuned models win
paragraphs: For high-volume, well-defined tasks, a fine-tuned model is usually cheaper to run and easier to control. At around 100,000 documents a month, fine-tuned inference infrastructure runs roughly $200 a month, versus roughly $5,000 a month with GPT-4o.

blocks.heading: When LLM-based NLP wins
paragraphs: For complex or rapidly changing tasks, low volumes, or when labeled training data is scarce, LLM-based NLP reaches production faster. Smaller models such as GPT-4o mini can keep per-document costs low.

blocks.heading: Measured before launch
paragraphs: Every system is validated on a held-out evaluation set using precision, recall and task-specific metrics, then monitored in production for drift.

items.question: What are natural language processing services?
items.answer: NLP services design and build software that understands text — classifying it, extracting entities and fields, measuring sentiment, summarizing it or searching it by meaning — and integrate that capability into your workflows and systems.

items.question: How much does custom NLP development cost?
items.answer: Custom NLP development costs $20,000–$250,000. The most common projects — text classification, named entity recognition and sentiment analysis — run $20,000–$70,000. Enterprise multi-task platforms run $80,000–$250,000.

items.question: How long does an NLP project take?
items.answer: Most focused NLP projects take 6–18 weeks depending on the task. Enterprise NLP platforms take 16–30 weeks.

items.question: Should we use a fine-tuned model or an LLM API?
items.answer: It depends on volume and task complexity. At high volume, fine-tuned models are usually far cheaper to run; for complex tasks, low volume or limited training data, LLM-based approaches reach production faster. We model both during discovery.

items.question: Do we need labeled training data?
items.answer: Fine-tuned models need labeled examples; we assess what you have and can run annotation with documented guidelines. LLM-based approaches can often start with few or no labeled examples, plus an evaluation set.

items.question: Who owns the NLP models?
items.answer: You do — model weights, training and inference code, labeled datasets and documentation are transferred at completion.
